skills.name: 21st-ui-build
skills.use: Build substantial UI using project context and grounded 21st inspiration.
skills.why: Reuse existing design primitives and preserve the product identity.
skills.requirements: 21st CLI or equivalent MCP tools; relevant access; explicit authority for paid generation or dependency changes.

skills.name: babysit
skills.use: Carry approved changes through PR checks, independent review, and merge.
skills.why: Keep delivery engaged until the requested result is verified.
skills.requirements: Git; GitHub CLI or equivalent; review-agent capability when requested.
skills.source: Personal maintained suite; earlier upstream provenance not recorded

skills.name: blast-radius
skills.use: Trace downstream effects of a proposed change or diff.
skills.why: Find affected callers, formats, configuration, and lifecycle assumptions.
skills.requirements: Repository access; existing checks where available.
skills.license: MIT upstream influence; locally rewritten workflow

skills.name: bug-hunter
skills.use: Run evidence-backed code and security reviews, with a Svelte-first lens.
skills.why: Separate reachable defects from speculation and refactoring preferences.
skills.requirements: Node.js 22+ for structured runtime; Git; optional current documentation/advisory access.

skills.name: codebase-design
skills.use: Design small interfaces that hide useful complexity.
skills.why: Keep behavior and maintenance knowledge local to a clear boundary.
skills.requirements: Project source and caller context.

skills.name: create-verification-skill
skills.use: Build project-local launch, drive, and proof instructions.
skills.why: Give future agents a repeatable way to exercise real behavior.
skills.requirements: The project runtime and its actual browser, CLI, API, or library driver.
skills.license: MIT upstream influence; locally rewritten workflow

skills.name: diagnosing-bugs
skills.use: Diagnose a reported failure or performance regression.
skills.why: Find discriminating evidence before changing code.
skills.requirements: A concrete symptom and access to the relevant implementation or runtime.

skills.name: docx-tracked-changes
skills.use: Report, accept, or reject supported inline Word revisions.
skills.why: Preserve restored text and original files while resolving revisions.
skills.requirements: Python 3; lxml; python-docx for regression tests; a document renderer for layout verification.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.use: Find and assess existing reusable skills.
skills.why: Reuse an appropriate maintained workflow instead of reinventing it.
skills.requirements: Web/source access; Node.js and the Skills CLI only for CLI-based discovery or installation.

skills.name: impeccable
skills.use: Improve frontend hierarchy, typography, accessibility, and interaction.
skills.why: Make design decisions deliberate and grounded in the project.
skills.requirements: Frontend source; browser access for live verification; optional tools described by the skill.

skills.name: improve-codebase-architecture
skills.use: Compare caller-first designs for a concrete architectural problem.
skills.why: Recommend an improvement grounded in actual callers and constraints.
skills.requirements: Project source; codebase-design is a useful companion.

skills.name: install-anti-slop
skills.use: Install bundled anti-slop Oxlint rules into an authorized project.
skills.why: Enforce selected recurring code-quality rules mechanically.
skills.requirements: A compatible JavaScript/TypeScript project and its package manager; see the bundled version requirements.
skills.license: Bundled rule sources: MIT; wrapper is a personal-suite edition

skills.name: maintain-verification-skill
skills.use: Check and update a project verification skill and feature map.
skills.why: Keep verification instructions aligned with source and live behavior.
skills.requirements: An existing project verification skill and the relevant runtime/driver.
skills.license: MIT upstream influence; locally rewritten workflow

skills.name: pdf-reader
skills.use: Read, search, and selectively render local PDF pages.
skills.why: Combine page-numbered text with visual evidence when layout matters.
skills.requirements: Python 3; Poppler: pdfinfo, pdftotext, and pdftoppm.

skills.name: project-audit
skills.use: Coordinate a scoped audit across code, tests, security, UX, and architecture.
skills.why: Produce one evidence-backed report with honest coverage and limits.
skills.requirements: Applicable bundled skills; project-specific checks; live drivers for runtime claims.
skills.source: Personal maintained suite; earlier upstream provenance not recorded

skills.name: punchlist
skills.use: Audit UI against named defects with locations and evidence.
skills.why: Turn design criticism into concrete, assessable findings.
skills.requirements: Suitable rendered/screenshot input; independent critics when required by its protocol; Python helpers; optional report tooling.

skills.name: redesign-existing-projects
skills.use: Improve an existing frontend while preserving its functionality.
skills.why: Replace generic or weak visual patterns using the existing stack.
skills.requirements: Project frontend and a rendered browser for meaningful visual verification.

skills.name: reflect
skills.use: Review selected completed work and recurring corrections.
skills.why: Propose small durable improvements rather than accumulating generic rules.
skills.requirements: Selected conversation/task evidence; history tools are optional.
skills.license: MIT upstream influence; locally rewritten workflow

skills.name: slice-loop-workflow
skills.use: Execute an ordered specification through implementation, PR review, merge, and Obsidian closeout.
skills.why: Keep each slice tied to acceptance criteria and record verified completion before starting the next.
skills.requirements: A canonical specification and handoff; a declared Obsidian vault; Git/PR tools; independent review capability; explicit authorization for repository and live effects.
skills.source: Personal maintained suite; portable edition of the existing Slice Loop workflow

skills.name: svelte-best-practices
skills.use: Apply modern Svelte 5 and SvelteKit patterns.
skills.why: Respect reactivity, ownership, SSR, accessibility, and server boundaries.
skills.requirements: A Svelte/SvelteKit project; current official docs for version-sensitive decisions.

skills.name: testprune
skills.use: Audit or improve a noisy, slow, redundant, or unsafe test suite.
skills.why: Preserve meaningful invariants and trustworthy offline verification.
skills.requirements: Python 3 for inventory; the project test runner; explicit invocation where the host honors that policy.

skills.name: typesafe-ai
skills.use: Compose typed AI judgments and probabilities with application code.
skills.why: Keep workflow logic in code while using AI for semantic decisions.
skills.requirements: Current TypeSafe documentation; credentials and service access for explicitly authorized API work.

skills.name: unclaimed
skills.use: Find and refresh single-word domain availability and pricing.
skills.why: Use the supporting CLI rather than guessing availability.
skills.requirements: Unclaimed CLI; network access; optional registrar configuration.

skills.name: ux-audit
skills.use: Exercise real user journeys in a live application.
skills.why: Find task-level confusion, blockers, and recovery problems.
skills.requirements: A real app instance; a supported browser driver; authorized test state.

skills.name: web-debug
skills.use: Reproduce frontend failures and verify fixes in a real browser.
skills.why: Connect actual interactions, console/network evidence, and observable outcomes.
skills.requirements: A browser automation tool supplied by the active agent; relevant local/staging access.

skills.name: youtube-transcript
skills.use: Retrieve YouTube captions with timestamps and source links.
skills.why: Summarize or search spoken content without a paid transcription service.
skills.requirements: Python 3; yt-dlp; network access; existing video captions.
